supply_chain_regulations.title: Define Security Requirements for Software Development
supply_chain_regulations.description: Organizations must define security requirements for their software development infrastructure and processes. This includes establishing policies for secure coding standards, security tooling requirements, and acceptable risk thresholds. Security requirements should be derived from regulatory obligations, industry standards, and organizational risk assessments. These requirements form the foundation for all subsequent SSDF practices.
requirements: Identify and document organizational security requirements
Specify security requirements for third-party components
Define acceptable risk thresholds for software releases
Establish secure coding standards and guidelines
Document compliance requirements (regulatory, contractual, industry)
supply_chain_regulations.applicability: All organizations developing software. Foundation practice required by EO 14028 self-attestation.
supply_chain_regulations.enforcement: Required for EO 14028 compliance (OMB M-22-18, M-23-16). Self-attestation by software producers.

supply_chain_regulations.title: Implement Roles and Responsibilities
supply_chain_regulations.description: Organizations must define and assign roles and responsibilities for secure software development activities. This includes designating security champions within development teams, establishing accountability for security decisions, and ensuring adequate security expertise is available. Clear role definitions prevent gaps in security coverage and ensure that someone is accountable for each security-relevant activity in the SDLC.
requirements: Define security roles within development teams
Assign accountability for security decisions and activities
Ensure security expertise is available for development teams
Establish security champion or security lead roles
Document escalation procedures for security concerns
supply_chain_regulations.applicability: All organizations developing software.
supply_chain_regulations.enforcement: Required for EO 14028 self-attestation. Organizational capability requirement.

supply_chain_regulations.title: Implement Supporting Toolchains
supply_chain_regulations.description: Organizations must deploy, configure, and maintain tools that support secure software development throughout the SDLC. This includes source code management systems, build systems, testing tools (SAST, DAST, SCA), artifact repositories, and CI/CD pipelines. Tools must be properly configured, kept updated, and their security verified. The toolchain itself is part of the attack surface and must be secured.
requirements: Deploy and maintain source code management with access controls
Implement automated build systems with integrity controls
Deploy security testing tools (SAST, DAST, SCA, secret scanning)
Maintain artifact repositories with access controls and integrity verification
Secure CI/CD pipeline configuration and credentials
supply_chain_regulations.applicability: All organizations developing software. Toolchain requirements scale with organizational size and risk.
supply_chain_regulations.enforcement: Required for EO 14028 self-attestation. Tool deployment is verifiable.

supply_chain_regulations.title: Define and Use Criteria for Software Security Checks
supply_chain_regulations.description: Organizations must define criteria for security checks at each stage of the SDLC, including quality gates that software must pass before proceeding. These criteria should cover threat modeling requirements, security testing coverage thresholds, vulnerability severity limits, and compliance validation. Clear criteria ensure consistent security decisions and prevent subjective trade-offs between security and delivery timelines.
requirements: Define security quality gates for each SDLC phase
Establish vulnerability severity thresholds for release decisions
Define security testing coverage requirements
Create criteria for threat model completeness
Document exception and waiver processes for quality gate bypasses
supply_chain_regulations.applicability: All organizations developing software. Criteria should be risk-proportionate.
supply_chain_regulations.enforcement: Required for EO 14028 self-attestation. Criteria documentation is auditable.

supply_chain_regulations.title: Implement and Maintain Secure Environments for Software Development
supply_chain_regulations.description: Organizations must ensure that development, build, and distribution environments are secure and that their integrity is maintained. This includes hardening development workstations, securing build servers, protecting signing keys, and isolating production environments from development. Environment security is critical because compromise of the development environment enables supply chain attacks at scale.
requirements: Harden development environments (workstations, VMs, containers)
Secure build servers and CI/CD infrastructure
Protect signing keys in HSMs or secure key management systems
Implement access controls and audit logging for all environments
Isolate production, staging, development, and build environments
supply_chain_regulations.applicability: All organizations developing software. Environment security is a foundation for all other practices.
supply_chain_regulations.enforcement: Required for EO 14028 self-attestation. Environment configuration is auditable.

supply_chain_regulations.title: Protect All Forms of Code from Unauthorized Access and Tampering
supply_chain_regulations.description: Organizations must implement controls to prevent unauthorized access to and tampering with all forms of code, including source code, build scripts, IaC templates, and configuration files. This includes using version control with access controls, implementing branch protection rules, requiring code review, and securing code repositories against unauthorized modification. Source code integrity is the foundation of supply chain security.
requirements: Store all code in version-controlled repositories with access controls
Implement branch protection rules requiring review before merge
Prevent direct pushes to main/production branches
Use commit signing to verify author identity
Monitor repositories for unauthorized access or modification
supply_chain_regulations.applicability: All organizations developing software. Applies to source code, IaC, configuration, and build scripts.
supply_chain_regulations.enforcement: Required for EO 14028 self-attestation. Repository configuration is verifiable.

supply_chain_regulations.title: Provide a Mechanism for Verifying Software Release Integrity
supply_chain_regulations.description: Organizations must provide mechanisms that allow consumers to verify the integrity of software releases. This includes cryptographic signing of release artifacts, publishing checksums, and providing signature verification instructions. Integrity verification enables consumers to detect tampering that may have occurred during distribution, a critical defense against supply chain attacks targeting the distribution channel.
requirements: Cryptographically sign all released software artifacts
Publish checksums (SHA-256 or stronger) for all releases
Provide public keys or certificate chains for signature verification
Document signature verification procedures for consumers
Use hardware-backed key management for signing keys
supply_chain_regulations.applicability: All organizations distributing software. Essential for supply chain trust.
supply_chain_regulations.enforcement: Required for EO 14028 self-attestation. Signature availability is verifiable.

supply_chain_regulations.title: Archive and Protect Each Software Release
supply_chain_regulations.description: Organizations must securely archive each software release along with its provenance information, SBOM, build configuration, and any security-relevant metadata. Archives must be protected against tampering and retained for the software's support lifetime. This enables consumers to verify past releases, supports incident investigation, and satisfies regulatory retention requirements (e.g., EU CRA's 10-year retention).
requirements: Archive all released software artifacts with integrity protection
Include provenance information, SBOM, and build metadata in archives
Protect archives against unauthorized modification or deletion
Define and implement retention policies aligned with support period
Enable retrieval of archived releases for verification or audit
supply_chain_regulations.applicability: All organizations distributing software.
supply_chain_regulations.enforcement: Required for EO 14028 self-attestation. Archive existence and integrity are auditable.

supply_chain_regulations.title: Design Software to Meet Security Requirements and Mitigate Security Risks
supply_chain_regulations.description: Organizations must incorporate security considerations into software design, including threat modeling, security architecture review, and applying secure design principles. Threat modeling should identify potential supply chain attack vectors, and the design should incorporate defenses against them. Secure design includes input validation, least privilege, defense in depth, secure defaults, and fail-safe error handling.
requirements: Conduct threat modeling during design phase
Apply secure design principles (least privilege, defense in depth, etc.)
Review architecture for security weaknesses before implementation
Document security design decisions and their rationale
Consider supply chain attack vectors in threat models
supply_chain_regulations.applicability: All software development. Applies from initial design through architectural changes.
supply_chain_regulations.enforcement: Required for EO 14028 self-attestation. Design artifacts are auditable.
supply_chain_regulations.keywords: design,threat modeling,architecture,security principles,least privilege,defense in depth

supply_chain_regulations.title: Reuse Existing, Well-Secured Software When Feasible
supply_chain_regulations.description: Organizations should reuse well-secured, well-maintained software components rather than creating new ones. When reusing third-party components, organizations must evaluate the security posture of those components, including their maintenance status, vulnerability history, and supply chain practices. This practice reduces the attack surface by leveraging vetted implementations while managing the risk of dependency on external code.
requirements: Evaluate security posture of third-party components before adoption
Assess maintenance status and community health of open source dependencies
Review vulnerability history and disclosure practices
Verify component provenance and supply chain integrity where possible
Maintain an inventory (SBOM) of all reused components
supply_chain_regulations.applicability: All organizations using third-party libraries, frameworks, or components.
supply_chain_regulations.enforcement: Required for EO 14028 self-attestation. Component evaluation records are auditable.

supply_chain_regulations.title: Create Source Code by Adhering to Secure Coding Practices
supply_chain_regulations.description: Developers must follow secure coding practices that prevent the introduction of common vulnerability classes. This includes following language-specific security guidelines, avoiding known-dangerous functions, performing input validation, using parameterized queries, and implementing proper error handling. Secure coding practices are the first line of defense against vulnerability introduction and should be enforced through linting, SAST tools, and code review.
requirements: Follow language-specific secure coding guidelines
Use parameterized queries to prevent injection vulnerabilities
Implement proper input validation and output encoding
Avoid known-dangerous functions and patterns
Apply secure error handling that does not leak sensitive information
supply_chain_regulations.applicability: All software developers. Language-specific guidelines apply per technology stack.
supply_chain_regulations.enforcement: Required for EO 14028 self-attestation. Coding standards and SAST results are auditable.
supply_chain_regulations.keywords: secure coding,coding standards,input validation,injection,error handling,best practices

supply_chain_regulations.title: Configure the Compilation, Interpreter, and Build Processes to Improve Executable Security
supply_chain_regulations.description: Organizations must configure compilers, interpreters, and build tools to maximize the security of the resulting executables. This includes enabling compiler security features (stack canaries, ASLR, DEP/NX), using hardened build flags, stripping debug symbols from release builds, and enabling runtime security mechanisms. Proper build configuration significantly reduces the exploitability of vulnerabilities that may exist in the code.
requirements: Enable compiler security features (stack protection, ASLR, DEP/NX)
Use hardened build flags appropriate to the language and platform
Strip debug symbols and unnecessary information from release builds
Configure runtime security mechanisms (seccomp, AppArmor, SELinux)
Verify build configuration through automated checks in CI/CD
supply_chain_regulations.applicability: All organizations building compiled software. Interpreted languages apply runtime hardening.
supply_chain_regulations.enforcement: Required for EO 14028 self-attestation. Build configuration is verifiable.

supply_chain_regulations.title: Review and/or Analyze Human-Readable Code to Identify Vulnerabilities and Verify Compliance with Security Requirements
supply_chain_regulations.description: Organizations must conduct code reviews and automated analysis of source code to identify vulnerabilities before release. This includes peer code review, automated SAST scanning, manual security code review for high-risk components, and verification that the code meets the defined security requirements. Code review is the primary mechanism for catching security issues that automated tools miss.
requirements: Conduct peer code review for all changes to production code
Run SAST tools automatically on all code changes
Perform manual security review for high-risk or security-critical code
Verify compliance with secure coding standards through automated checks
Document and track findings from code reviews and analysis
supply_chain_regulations.applicability: All organizations developing software. Review depth proportionate to risk.
supply_chain_regulations.enforcement: Required for EO 14028 self-attestation. Review records and SAST reports are auditable.

supply_chain_regulations.title: Test Executable Code to Identify Vulnerabilities and Verify Compliance with Security Requirements
supply_chain_regulations.description: Organizations must test compiled or packaged software for vulnerabilities using dynamic analysis techniques. This includes DAST scanning, fuzzing, penetration testing, and integration security testing. Dynamic testing catches vulnerability classes that static analysis misses, such as configuration errors, authentication bypass, race conditions, and memory corruption issues that only manifest at runtime.
requirements: Run DAST tools against deployed or running software
Perform fuzzing on input-processing components
Conduct penetration testing on security-critical software
Test for common vulnerability classes (OWASP Top 10, CWE Top 25)
Verify that security controls function as designed through testing
supply_chain_regulations.applicability: All organizations developing software that will be deployed. Testing scope proportionate to risk.
supply_chain_regulations.enforcement: Required for EO 14028 self-attestation. Test results are auditable.

supply_chain_regulations.title: Configure Software to Have Secure Settings by Default
supply_chain_regulations.description: Software must be configured with secure settings by default upon installation. Users should not need to perform additional hardening steps to achieve a baseline secure configuration. Default configurations should follow the principle of least functionality, disabling unnecessary features, ports, protocols, and services. This practice reduces the attack surface for software as deployed and aligns with EU CRA requirements for secure-by-default.
requirements: Ship software with secure-by-default configuration
Disable unnecessary features, ports, and services by default
Apply principle of least functionality in default configurations
Document any security-relevant configuration changes from defaults
Provide hardening guides for further security customization
supply_chain_regulations.applicability: All software that includes configurable settings affecting security.
supply_chain_regulations.enforcement: Required for EO 14028 self-attestation. Default configuration is testable.

framework_mappings.EU_CRA: Annex I Part I (secure by default)

supply_chain_regulations.keywords: secure defaults,configuration,hardening,least functionality,out of box,attack surface

supply_chain_regulations.title: Identify and Confirm Vulnerabilities on an Ongoing Basis
supply_chain_regulations.description: Organizations must continuously monitor for and identify vulnerabilities in their software and its dependencies. This includes monitoring vulnerability databases (NVD, OSV, GitHub Advisories), conducting regular security assessments, accepting and triaging external vulnerability reports, and performing software composition analysis. Ongoing identification is critical because new vulnerabilities are discovered continuously in both proprietary and third-party code.
requirements: Monitor vulnerability databases for known vulnerabilities in dependencies
Accept and triage vulnerability reports from external researchers
Conduct regular security assessments and penetration tests
Run SCA tools to match dependencies against vulnerability databases
Establish a coordinated vulnerability disclosure process
supply_chain_regulations.applicability: All organizations developing and maintaining software. Continuous activity throughout software lifecycle.
supply_chain_regulations.enforcement: Required for EO 14028 self-attestation. Monitoring and response processes are auditable.

supply_chain_regulations.title: Assess, Prioritize, and Remediate Vulnerabilities
supply_chain_regulations.description: Organizations must assess the severity and exploitability of identified vulnerabilities, prioritize them based on risk, and remediate them within defined timeframes. Prioritization should consider CVSS scores, known exploitation status (CISA KEV catalog), reachability analysis, and business impact. Remediation may include patching, configuration changes, compensating controls, or accepting the risk with documented justification.
requirements: Assess vulnerability severity using CVSS and other risk factors
Prioritize remediation based on exploitability and business impact
Define SLA timelines for vulnerability remediation by severity
Track remediation progress and report metrics
Document risk acceptance decisions for unpatched vulnerabilities
supply_chain_regulations.applicability: All organizations developing and maintaining software.
supply_chain_regulations.enforcement: Required for EO 14028 self-attestation. Remediation metrics and risk decisions are auditable.

supply_chain_regulations.title: Analyze Vulnerabilities to Identify Their Root Causes
supply_chain_regulations.description: Organizations must analyze remediated vulnerabilities to understand their root causes and prevent similar vulnerabilities from being introduced in the future. Root cause analysis should identify systemic issues in development practices, tooling gaps, training needs, or architectural weaknesses. Lessons learned should be fed back into security requirements (PO.1), coding standards (PW.5), and quality gate criteria (PO.4).
requirements: Conduct root cause analysis for significant vulnerabilities
Identify systemic issues in development practices or tools
Update secure coding guidelines based on findings
Improve security testing to catch similar vulnerability classes
Feed lessons learned back into training and awareness programs
supply_chain_regulations.applicability: All organizations developing software. Root cause analysis depth proportionate to vulnerability severity and frequency.
supply_chain_regulations.enforcement: Required for EO 14028 self-attestation. Root cause analysis records are auditable.
supply_chain_regulations.keywords: root cause analysis,lessons learned,systemic issues,prevention,continuous improvement

supply_chain_regulations.title: Coordinated Vulnerability Disclosure Process
supply_chain_regulations.description: Organizations must establish a process for receiving, triaging, and responding to vulnerability reports from external researchers, customers, and other stakeholders. The process should include a public vulnerability disclosure policy (security.txt per RFC 9116), defined response timeframes, and provisions for coordinated disclosure with the reporter. This practice enables the security community to contribute to the organization's security posture.
requirements: Publish a vulnerability disclosure policy (security.txt recommended)
Provide a secure channel for receiving vulnerability reports (e.g., encrypted email, HackerOne)
Acknowledge reports within a defined timeframe (recommended: 5 business days)
Coordinate disclosure timeline with the reporter
Publish security advisories for confirmed vulnerabilities
supply_chain_regulations.applicability: All organizations developing and distributing software.
supply_chain_regulations.enforcement: Required for EO 14028 self-attestation. Disclosure policy existence is verifiable.

supply_chain_regulations.title: Communicate Vulnerability Information to Stakeholders
supply_chain_regulations.description: Organizations must communicate vulnerability information, patches, and mitigations to affected users and stakeholders in a timely manner. Communication channels include security advisories, mailing lists, CVE publications, and automated notification systems. For supply chain contexts, downstream consumers who integrate the affected software must be notified so they can assess their own exposure and take appropriate action.
requirements: Publish security advisories for all vulnerabilities in supported releases
Assign CVE identifiers for publicly disclosed vulnerabilities
Provide clear remediation guidance (patches, workarounds, mitigations)
Notify downstream users through established channels (mailing lists, advisories)
Communicate severity, impact, and affected versions clearly
supply_chain_regulations.applicability: All organizations distributing software. Communication urgency proportionate to severity.
supply_chain_regulations.enforcement: Required for EO 14028 self-attestation. Advisory publication history is verifiable.
